task: Draft an AI-research grant application using only verified facts — leave any unknown field blank rather than inventing it.
project_summary: A small research group is applying for an AI-safety research grant. The application needs a project summary, methodology, budget justification, and team bios, within strict word limits and using only facts the group has confirmed.
current_direction: Assemble a first full draft from confirmed facts, clearly marking every field that still needs a real answer from the applicants.

decisions.title: Never invent applicant facts
decisions.body: Any figure, affiliation, date, or credential that isn't in the verified facts must be left as an explicit blank for the applicants to fill.
decisions.rationale: A grant application is a factual, accountable document; a fabricated detail can void it and damage trust.
decisions.tradeoffs: The first draft will have visible gaps, which is correct — gaps are honest, invented facts are not.

decisions.title: Respect the funder's word limits per section
decisions.body: Summary <= 200 words; methodology <= 500 words; each bio <= 100 words.
decisions.rationale: Over-limit sections are commonly rejected unread.

evidence.claim: Funders routinely enforce per-section word limits and reject over-limit submissions

sources.label: Grants.gov — Grant writing guidance
sources.bound_claim: Funders routinely enforce per-section word limits

constraints: Use only the verified facts listed; mark everything else as [NEEDS APPLICANT INPUT].
Do not exceed any section's word limit.
Do not claim results, partnerships, or funding that are not in the verified facts.
boundaries: Draft prose only; do not submit anything or fill the funder's portal.
Do not add applicant personal data beyond what is provided.
what_to_avoid: Inventing plausible-sounding metrics, affiliations, or prior awards.
Padding a section to hit a word count with filler.
open_questions: What is the confirmed total budget figure and its breakdown?
Which team members have consented to be named, and with what titles?
Is there a confirmed institutional partner, or should that stay blank?
next_steps: Draft the project summary from the confirmed problem statement.
Draft the methodology, marking any unconfirmed step as [NEEDS APPLICANT INPUT].
List each required field the applicants must still supply before submission.
definition_of_done: A complete draft within every word limit, where each fact traces to the verified list and every unknown is an explicit, labelled blank — not an invention.

recommended_assistant.reason: This is structured, constraint-bound prose drafting, not coding or open research.
